rv.q: For all Maxwell's perceptivity about loneliness, loss and dogs, and for all Young's vulnerability and charm, the world of Man's Best Friend is neither close enough nor far away enough to hit where it hurts.

Deeply moving but disjointed one-man play about grief and dogs Douglas Maxwell is a prolific playwright, having penned more than 40 plays since 2000. He is in a particularly purple patch at the moment, picking up best new play at the Critics’ Awards for Theatre in Scotland two years in a row.
